## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vacchanakhajātaka* (Ja 235) is a canonical birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection in the Khuddaka Nikāya. According to the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the Buddha delivered the discourse while residing at Jetavana concerning Roja the Mallian (*Roja Malla*), a lay friend of the Venerable Ānanda [Fausböll 1879; Freedman 1977]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was living as the wandering ascetic (*paribbājaka* or *isi*) named Vacchanakha [Freedman 1977; Fausböll 1879; Fausböll 1897]. A wealthy merchant of Bārāṇasī (*Bārāṇasīseṭṭhi*), who was a friend of the ascetic, believed that the renouncer's life was full of suffering and sought to persuade Vacchanakha to leave the order and enjoy household pleasures with him, reciting the verse opening with *Sukhā gharā Vacchanakha* ("Houses in the world are sweet, Vacchanakha...") [Fausböll 1879; Freedman 1977]. The Bodhisatta countered by explaining the faults and perils of the household life before returning to his grove [Fausböll 1879]. In the story's identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha revealed that the merchant was Roja the Mallian and the wanderer Vacchanakha was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879; Freedman 1977]. The text is also cited in modern editorial apparatus to the Vinaya Piṭaka [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga].
